correctness.rationale: For bounded dipole strengths, the infinite operator is VDV*, where V synthesizes normalized coherent vectors and their normalized differences. Gaussian mixed derivatives and separation 20 prove 1/2 I <= V*V <= 3/2 I uniformly in every small displacement. Each exact two-by-two D block squares to the squared strength times identity, so bounded congruence sandwiches every singular value and proves the full compactness and Schatten characterization. Polynomial growth ensures absolute convergence of the stated polynomial-core form; the theorem does not assert unbounded-strength necessity. value.rationale: The positivity assumption is essential to existing Gaussian Fock local-mass characterizations. This theorem gives a natural full infinite-dimensional family of signed atomic forms whose positive/negative parts are not even bounded, yet the signed operator can be trace class; it determines the entire quasi-Schatten regularity scale with two-sided singular-value estimates rather than an isolated counterexample. The exact p=1/3 crossover is a motivated illustration of the spectral cancellation mechanism.
